rebuilds.why: Fault: hen, cat, dog read as kept animals and left snake, frog as a second odd pair. Cat and dog are replaced by cow and whale, so the only three sharing a rule are the egg-layers hen, snake, frog; no other three of the five form a group.

stem.prompt: Three of these words go together. Which two are the odd ones out?

options.execution: The child spots that cow does not lay eggs and stops there. Hen is paired with it because both live on a farm, but hen belongs to the egg-laying three.
The child picks out whale as one odd word and pairs it with snake, perhaps because neither has legs. Snake lays eggs, so it sits inside the group and cow is left out of the answer.
The child notices that snake and frog both lay eggs and offers them. That is the rule of the group, so these two belong; the child has answered which words go together instead of which two do not.

stem.prompt: Three of these words go together. Which two are the odd ones out?

options.execution: The child sees that ball is a thing rather than an action and stops there. Jump is added as its partner, but jump is one of the three movement words, so net is left out of the answer.
The child finds net as one odd word but pairs it with hop. Hop is a way of moving on your legs like jump and run, so it belongs to the group of three.
The child notices that jump and run are both ways of moving and offers them. Those two follow the group's own rule, so the child has answered which words belong instead of which two are odd.
